title: Aleksandr Savchenko
body: Welcome to my public working directory. This website is generated from the files in this repository. Browse it like a small, read-only filesystem: open a folder, read a document, or search everything at once.
snippet: Computer vision engineer building practical tools and sharing technical notes.

title: About me
body: I work in ADAS/AD automotive sector and develop production software in c/c++ for embedded systems. It includes Surround View systems, camera views, algorithms, etc. Connect GitHub LinkedIn About this site I use emacs (spacemacs) as my main editor for more than a decade. I do like the style, dired mode and other features. \\ And my idea was to try to create a website which is generated from my org-mode files right away, also in dired style. Here you can use vim motions and use search with preview via s button.
snippet: Computer vision engineer.

title: Raw Pixel Viewer
body: Raw Pixel Viewer Raw Pixel Viewer opens camera and image buffers directly in the browser. It supports common raw layouts such as NV12, planar YUV, packed YUV422, Bayer RAW, RGB, and grayscale data. Files are decoded locally and never uploaded. Open the live tool Supported formats YUV semi-planar: NV12, NV21, NV16, NV61, and P010, including 10 to 16-bit data in 16-bit words, little or big endian. YUV planar: I420 (YUV420P), YV12, YUV422P, and YVU422P, including high bit depth variants such as yuv420p10le. YUV packed: YUYV (YUY2) and UYVY, with BT.601, BT.709, or BT.2020 matrices in limited or full range. Bayer RAW: RGGB, BGGR, GRBG, and GBRG; 8-bit, 10 to 16-bit in 16-bit words, and packed MIPI RAW10 and RAW12. RGB and grayscale: RGB24, BGR24, RGBA32, BGRA32, ARGB32, ABGR32, GRAY8, and GRAY16. Images: PNG, JPEG, and BMP, for comparing a raw buffer with a reference. How to view an NV12 file 1. Open the tool and drop the .yuv or .raw file onto the page. 2. Choose NV12 under YUV layouts and enter the width and height. For NV12 the file is width × height × 1.5 bytes per frame. 3. If the picture looks sheared, set the stride. If the colors look wrong, try NV21 or swap U and V. Guess format tries common sizes and layouts for you. Tools Split, grid, wipe, and diff views; linked zoom; per-pixel values; RGB and luma histograms; and PNG or JPEG export.
snippet: Inspect raw NV12, YUV, Bayer, RGB, and grayscale pixel buffers directly in the browser.

title: Sync Reader
body: Sync Reader Sync Reader is a parallel text reader for learning German with Russian translations. It lets you read bilingual texts side by side, inspect words in context, save useful vocabulary, and export it for Anki. Open the live tool Why I built it The main idea is to see a word immediately in sentence context instead of only seeing a direct translation. You can also read the text first in your native language and then in the language you are learning. The app stays serverless: no account, subscription, or paid usage limit. Texts, folders, saved words, and study data are stored locally in the browser. Features Parallel Russian and German reading panes. Linked highlighting across both texts: click or hover a word to see its translation and grammar notes. Saved vocabulary and Anki-style review. TSV export for Anki. A local library with folders and browser storage. 26 built-in texts at A2 and B1 level on everyday life, money, technology, work, and travel. Import of plain-text files generated by an LLM, with problems reported per line. How to add your own text 1. Open the tool and choose Add text. Describe the topic and level, then copy the prompt into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini. 2. Paste the whole reply back into the app and save it. Each sentence is a DE: line and an RU: line, and linked words are marked like [den Schrank]4 with the same number on both sides. 3. To import texts you already have, drop .txt files or a whole folder onto the app. A folder becomes a library folder, and any broken lines are listed with their line numbers.
snippet: A local-first parallel reader for learning German with Russian translations.

title: Welcome
body: Hey! I'm Aleksandr Savchenko. Welcome to my blog! \\ Here I do experiments with website in emacs-like style, host static web tools and post notes. I am a computer vision engineer working on perception software, including classical and CNN approaches. Interested in things about ISP, camera systems, image processing, rendering, detection algorithms. \\ \\ ls --highlights :dashboard: projects/ - raw-pixel-viewer/ :: Raw pixel viewer to open NV12, YUV, Bayer images. More convenient version of old rawpixels app - sync-reader/ :: German and Russian parallel reader for language learning, including anki style repetition. notes/ - automotive/ :: Mostly videos about Surround View systems. - computer-vision/ :: Calibration, fisheye tools, and github projects. - papers/ :: Interesting papers to read.
snippet: Homepage welcome text.
